name: FAME

paper.title: Principled Fast and Meta Knowledge Learners for Continual Reinforcement Learning

construction.unit: a (state, action) pair from the last N steps of training on a task (MinAtar N = 12,000, 2.4% of the task's steps)
construction.kept_as: raw states with the actions the fast learner took (states only for FAME-WD); no rewards
construction.processing: a fast learner (DQN, PPO or SAC) trains on the current task; its final N steps are copied into the meta buffer; after the task a meta learner is refit to all stored pairs by maximum likelihood (FAME-KL) or a Wasserstein loss (FAME-WD)
construction.writer: rule: store the last N steps; supervised refit of the meta network

organization.structure: two learners: a fast learner for the current task (own replay buffer F, cleared per task) and a meta learner that holds all past tasks, fed by a fixed-size meta buffer M
organization.stores: meta buffer M (100k pairs MinAtar, 200k Atari); fast buffer F; fast and meta network weights

management.operations: after each task: refit the meta learner on old pairs plus the new task's pairs (new pairs sampled every k-th batch so each task weighs the same), then append the new pairs to M
management.conflicts: the refit minimises the policy divergence to every past task at once (forgetting as KL or W2 between policies)
management.forgetting: M is a FIFO deque; with 7 tasks × 12,000 pairs it never fills on MinAtar

retrieval.query: the first steps of a new task
retrieval.candidates: three initialisations: previous fast learner, meta learner, random network
retrieval.selection: run fast and meta greedily for n steps each and keep the higher mean return (or a one-sided t-test); a random network is compared by its Q-value at the start state in the code
retrieval.budget: n = 600 steps per candidate on MinAtar, 1,200 on Atari, 10 episodes on Meta-World

use.context: no text context: the chosen learner initialises or regularises the new fast learner
use.reasoning: meta chosen: BC regulariser KL(meta ‖ fast) for the first L = 50k steps (λ = 1); fast chosen: keep fine-tuning; random: reset

classify.note: Fast learner (current task) and meta learner (all tasks) are two tiers; a small buffer of past (state, action) pairs is consolidated into the meta network after each task. At a new task all candidate learners are evaluated and the best by mean return (top-1) is used.

stages.ingestion: Tasks arrive one at a time with known boundaries and a fixed step budget (500k steps per MinAtar task, 1M on Atari and Meta-World).
stages.construction: During the last N steps of a task the fast learner's (state, action) pairs are copied to the meta buffer (N = 12,000 on MinAtar, 20,000 on Atari).
stages.organization: Two learners of the same architecture: a fast learner trained by RL on the current task, and a meta learner meant to hold every past task, fed by one fixed-size meta buffer.
stages.update: After each task the meta learner is refit by supervised learning on all stored pairs (MLE on softmax policies for FAME-KL, a Gaussian W2 loss against the previous meta and current fast policies for FAME-WD).
stages.retrieval: When a new task starts, the previous fast learner and the meta learner are each run for n steps and compared with a random network; the best becomes the warm start.
stages.answer: If the meta learner wins, the fast learner is trained with a KL behaviour-cloning term toward the meta policy for the first L steps; the final evaluation uses the meta learner.
stages.learning: Fast learner: DQN, PPO or SAC. Meta learner: supervised (NLL or W2) on the meta buffer, 200 epochs on MinAtar and Atari, 5,000 × k mini-batches on Meta-World.

summary: A hippocampus/neocortex-style pair for continual RL: a fast learner trains on each task, a meta learner is refit on a small buffer of every task's state-action pairs to minimise a policy-based forgetting measure, and each new task starts from whichever of fast, meta or random scores best in a short evaluation.
notes: VENUE: ICLR 2026 main (PDF header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'; OpenReview loNTDX3wTn lists 'ICLR 2026 Poster'). CODE: datake/FAME at d16f0061 (2026-02-28, one day before arXiv v1); MinAtar/FAME.py, Atari/run_ppo_FAME.py, Metaworld/test_main.py + agent/sac.py read. Figures follow the MinAtar code (the value-based algorithm of Alg. 1). MEMORY FRAMING: not an LLM memory; included as a parametric, two-tier procedural memory for RL agents. RESULTS: MinAtar and Atari scores are stored raw (return / unstated scale); Meta-World success, FT and forgetting are ×100.

sources.code_note: Official repo linked in the abstract; commit d16f0061 (2026-02-28) is the latest and predates arXiv v1 by one day. It holds separate scripts for MinAtar (DQN), Atari (PPO) and Meta-World (SAC). As released, MinAtar/FAME.py reads args.p_explore, which its parser never defines, so the script needs a fix before it runs.

headline: What is kept per task is only the (state, action) pairs of its last N steps, 2.4% of training on MinAtar; rewards are not stored.
The meta learner is a behaviour-cloned policy of all past fast learners, refit after every task; it is also the network that is scored at the end.
At a new task, stored knowledge is used only if the meta learner wins a short evaluation against the previous fast learner and a random network.

open_questions: The meta learner clones actions from ε-greedy rollouts of the fast learner, so random exploration actions are part of what it imitates; the paper does not discuss this.
Tasks repeat inside every MinAtar sequence, so part of the gain may come from recognising an old game via the warm-up test rather than from consolidation.

text: When a task starts, the previous fast learner and the meta learner each play 600 steps and the code scores a random network by its Q-value; the best one is the warm start.
If the meta learner wins, the kept fast learner is pulled toward it by a KL term for 50k steps; the evaluation steps count against the task budget.

discussion.takeaway: Split continual RL into a fast learner for the current task and a meta learner that is refit, after each task, to imitate all past tasks from a small buffer; start each task from whichever learner does best in a short test. On MinAtar, Atari modes and Meta-World this gives the highest average performance with little forgetting.

claims.claim: Minimising a policy-based forgetting measure gives a simple incremental rule: maximum likelihood on a mixture of past tasks' state-action distributions.
claims.evidence: Prop. 1 and Eq. 5 (value-based), Eq. 7 (KL), Prop. 2 / Eq. 8 (Wasserstein) (§3).

claims.claim: FAME beats all baselines on MinAtar.
claims.evidence: Table 1: average return 14.54 / 18.72 / 1.69 vs best baseline 10.71 / 4.95 / 1.16; forgetting 0.72 vs ≥ 1.25; FT 0.16 ties LargeBuffer.

claims.claim: The warm-up test picks the right prior knowledge.
claims.evidence: Fig. 2 right: meta chosen 95.1% on a seen game; random chosen 70.2% on a new one.
Table 3: Meta-World average success 0.767 (WD) and 0.733 (KL) vs 0.491 PackNet, forgetting 0.023 / 0.073.
Meta buffer ~1-2% of each task's data, same size as a standard replay buffer; meta refit takes minutes (App. E).

limits: One meta learner holds all knowledge; a learned latent representation might distil and reason better.
Other transfer techniques (e.g. context embeddings) are not explored.
Task boundaries must be known and all tasks must share state and action spaces.
reading: On Atari SpaceInvader modes, Finetune's forward transfer (0.65) is higher than FAME's (0.63), although the text says FAME beats all baselines on both metrics.

Baselines other than Finetune are reset at every task and have no access to past data except LargeBuffer, while FAME keeps a meta buffer and a second network; the paper argues the buffer matches the standard replay size, but Table 6 shows scores drop as N shrinks (Space Invaders 18.72 → 14.69 at N = 4,000).
MinAtar forgetting is normalised by each game's standard deviation across the compared methods, so the number depends on which baselines are in the table.
In the MinAtar code the random candidate is scored by an untrained network's Q-value, not by a return, so the three-way test compares returns with a Q estimate.
In the Meta-World code the warm start chooses only between a fresh agent and the meta actor; the previous fast policy is never a candidate, unlike the paper's description.
FAME-KL and FAME-WD are close on Meta-World (0.733 vs 0.767) and swap order on CW10 (0.370 vs 0.340), so neither divergence is clearly better.

abstract.text: The paper frames continual reinforcement learning after the brain's hippocampus-neocortex split. It defines a distance between MDPs and a measure of catastrophic forgetting, and builds FAME from two learners: a fast learner that learns the current task and a meta learner that, after each task, is refit on stored state-action pairs to minimise forgetting across all tasks seen so far. A new task starts from the previous fast learner, the meta learner or a random network, whichever wins a short evaluation, with a behaviour-cloning term when the meta learner is chosen. Experiments on MinAtar, Atari playing modes and Meta-World report better average performance and less forgetting than continual-RL baselines.
